races.name: Betway Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Loriko
runners_data.note: Arrives in excellent form with two consecutive wins on Good ground, races prominently and will likely lead from the off under Harry Skelton for a trainer firing at nearly 27% over 14 days; the step back up to 2m4½f suits on form and his sim-going record is strong — the STYLE_FIT tag is marginal here as leading is his natural register.

runners_data.name: Master Haku
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's charge brings strong Flat/bumper-to-hurdle form and placed comfortably at 2m on Good last time; Sean Bowen will aim to track the leader throughout and his two wins-plus-placed record in similar going makes him the most dangerous rival if Loriko flattens out late.

runners_data.name: Nobotheratall
runners_data.note: Has genuine winning form over 2m on Good — including a recent score 35 days ago — and is a confirmed front-runner by nature, but with Loriko certain to lead, he is likely to find himself further back than ideal and carrying the penalty for racing out of role; his chance depends heavily on whether he can get close enough to the pace from a position that doesn't suit him.

runners_data.name: Ballinoulart
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old whose recent form reads as a string of placed efforts without winning, a horse that naturally wants to race up with the pace but will be shuffled back into midfield by the race shape here; the 7lb claimer Richard Upton reduces the burden on OR 69 but a zero wins-from-five hurdles record in similar conditions limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Arcimboldo
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up horse with no wins or placed efforts on Turf Good going in his last five starts, all of which came on Standard Tapeta — the switch to Good turf and step up to 2m4½f are genuine unknowns; Charlie Maggs (3) claims 3lb but trainer Mike Sowersby has just 1 winner from 2 runners in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Show Your Hand
runners_data.note: Ran twice into second over 2m on Good already this season, so the going and approximate trip are well within range; headgear (tongue-tie) is retained and Freddie Keighley claims 5lb, but as a hold-up horse on a sustainable pace she will need Loriko to fade significantly for her finishing effort to reach the leaders in time.

races.paceDynamic: Loriko is the confirmed and uncontested pace-setter here, likely to stride on from the front under Harry Skelton and set a measured, controlled gallop on Good ground over 2m4½f — a trip that rewards horses who travel well through a race rather than those who need a strong end-to-end gallop to produce their best. Master Haku is the most dangerous immediate rival for the prominent pitch and may track Loriko closely throughout, while Arcimboldo and Show Your Hand will be ridden as genuine hold-up horses from the back. This field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Nobotheratall and Ballinoulart are natural front-runners who are likely to be shuffled back into midfield territory given Loriko's presence, meaning they are racing outside their comfort zone and carry that discount accordingly. A single, class front-runner setting a sustainable tempo on Good ground at Market Rasen — a track that already rewards galloping types — creates conditions that strongly favour horses who can travel prominently in behind the leader and quicken on the turn for home; genuine hold-up horses face a test of whether there is enough end-pace generated to bring them into it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Loriko Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Loriko is allowed a clear lead throughout and sets a controlled pace that stretches the field without breaking them
scenarios.body: Loriko travels within himself in front, builds a winning advantage at the last and Skelton times the quicken to perfection; Master Haku is best placed to give chase but the leader's form at this distance on Good ground is compelling.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Master Haku tracks Loriko relentlessly and pounces when Loriko weakens late
scenarios.body: Master Haku, with strong recent form including a win over 2m at Good, travels with zeal and outstays Loriko once the pressure increases after the last; Elliott's yard is in solid form and Bowen is adept at this tracking role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Best
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to bring Show Your Hand or Arcimboldo into contention off the back of a fast-run race
scenarios.body: Show Your Hand has placed twice over 2m on Good and Arcimboldo has shown progressive form, but both need a stronger gallop than a lone, class front-runner typically generates in a small field; a successful late challenge here would require Loriko to go off too fast and empty significantly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Causes Upset
scenarios.trigger: If either Nobotheratall or Ballinoulart manages to recover a more prominent position and races near their natural style
scenarios.body: Both are true prominent runners forced wide of their comfort zone by Loriko's presence; Nobotheratall has winning form on Good and has some claims if he can get close enough to the pace, but Ballinoulart's OR of 69 and zero wins in his last five hurdles starts make this the least likely route to an upset.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Master Haku immediately pressures Loriko after the first two hurdles — if Elliott's horse locks on to the leader, the contest is between those two from a long way out and the rest are racing for third.

Nobotheratall's early positioning is critical: if Harry Reed secures a slot just behind the leaders rather than dropping deep, his true-prominent profile reasserts itself and he becomes a live threat; watch the first half-mile for where he settles.

Show Your Hand's finishing effort depends entirely on the pace being strong enough to bring her into the race — on Good ground with only six runners and one honest front-runner, that end-pace may never materialise; watch if Keighley is forced to commit early.

Arcimboldo's whole profile is built on Standard Tapeta form at 2m — today's switch to Turf Good and the extra four-plus furlongs of distance means his form figures translate poorly; watch his jumping and how he travels in the first circuit for signs of comfort at the trip.

Ballinoulart's headgear (hood/p tag) may be a small market mover angle but the wider race context means he is effectively racing from a position he has no history of winning from — monitor his early stride pattern to gauge whether he can steal a prominent berth before Loriko asserts.

races.name: Betway Summer Handicap Hurdle Race (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Indemnity
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in fine course-type form with four wins and six places from 14 runs on Good going, but a 70-day absence for Emma Lavelle's yard whose 14-day record reads 0/3 raises a small freshness flag; needs to press from the front and gets crowded out if the early positions are contested fiercely.

runners_data.name: Moon Chime
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant here — this is her natural role; won two of her last five on similar going and trades the tactical burden of leading alone, which suits her but at 8 years old stamina at the top of the weights is not guaranteed against younger rivals.

runners_data.name: Howth
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type with four wins from 15 Good-ground starts and strong course-type figures; Tom Lacey's yard is 1/5 in the 14-day window and Brendan Powell has a clear track record over this sort of trip, giving this runner a solid chance of holding a genuine prominent position.

runners_data.name: Louis Veron
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a sharp upward trajectory — 2-2-1 in recent form, all on Good or Soft, and three wins from four Good-ground runs; Harry Skelton's booking for the Dan Skelton yard (7/26 in 14 days) is the most powerful jockey-trainer combination in the race and suggests serious intent from a horse with a natural prominent style.

runners_data.name: Newtown Rambler
runners_data.note: Relentless winning machine with five wins from nine Good-going runs including a hat-trick of recent victories; 20 days since last run is no bar for this consistent sort, and with the strong rider Oakley Brown claiming 5lb the effective weight is attractive — one of the most likely to physically secure a prominent berth despite the traffic.

runners_data.name: Continuance
runners_data.note: Placed in all five recent starts and genuinely wants to race up with the pace, but with six prominent types contesting four positions he is among those most likely to find himself shuffled back further than he'd like; Martin Keighley's yard is 0/4 in 14 days, and the STYLE_FIT friction (0.91) should temper expectations if he cannot get close early.

runners_data.name: Charlus
runners_data.note: One of only two genuine hold-up horses in the race, which is relevant given the prominent overcrowding; recent form reads FP0P-5 with no wins from 13 starts on similar going, and the headgear combination of hood and tongue-tie has not unlocked improvement — his chance relies on others making errors.

runners_data.name: Morning Mayhem
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's yard sends this prominent-style five-year-old who has won on Good ground, but he is among the overspill runners pushed into a midfield slot he does not naturally occupy; a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 is the best in the redistributed group, suggesting minimal positional disruption, yet the crowded conditions are still an inconvenience he must overcome.

runners_data.name: Pigeon House
runners_data.note: The other genuine hold-up runner alongside Charlus; won at 16f on Good ground and placed three times recently, with a pull in the weights that could matter; Lee Edwards rides and the yard's 14-day record is 0/3, so no trainer momentum — but as a true closer he at least races in his natural role, which is an advantage over many opponents.

runners_data.name: Squeezebox
runners_data.note: Four wins from nine Good-ground runs and strong class credentials for Tom Lacey's yard, which is 1/5 in 14 days; Stan Sheppard rides this horse who naturally wants to be prominent but is bumped into the midfield map — 46 days since last run is fine, and the form string (151-1) is excellent, but getting boxed in would compromise his chance significantly.

runners_data.name: Letterston Lily
runners_data.note: 86 days off the track is the longest layoff in the field, and while she won on Good ground over 2m4f her best form has come at a longer trip; Mickey Bowen's stable reads 0/8 in 14 days, adding a concern layer — her true prominent style is obscured by redistribution into midfield, meaning she must get a clear run to matter late.

runners_data.name: Mojito Des Mottes
runners_data.note: Four-year-old by far the youngest in the race, carrying the minimum 149lbs with Harry Cobden up, and 111 days off the track is the longest absence; showed form figures of 2-2-4-4 in recent starts, all on Good or Soft, and is another prominent type moved to midfield — Ben Pauling's 0/4 in 14 days is a quiet run-in, and the long absence limits confidence.

runners_data.name: High Fibre
runners_data.note: Wearing a visor and back just 8 days after his last run under Sean Bowen for James Owen's yard (8/48 in 14 days — high volume, useful strike rate); 12 wins and places from 15 Good-ground starts is excellent course-type data, and while he too is a natural prominent type mapped to midfield, the visor switch and quick return suggest connections see a target opportunity here.

races.paceDynamic: Moon Chime is the one confirmed front-runner and will attempt to lead from the outset, setting a sustainable but uncontested gallop on Good ground over 2m½f. However, this is a field loaded with prominent-racing types — Indemnity, Howth, Louis Veron, Newtown Rambler, Continuance, Morning Mayhem, Squeezebox, Letterston Lily, Mojito Des Mottes and High Fibre all want to race close to the pace, meaning several will be forced to settle further back than their natural inclination; Newtown Rambler and Louis Veron, with their stronger recent form and better jockey bookings, are the most likely to physically secure the prominent positions behind Moon Chime. The field contains far more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, so the displaced runners — particularly Continuance, Morning Mayhem, Squeezebox, Letterston Lily and Mojito Des Mottes — will be shuffled into uncharacteristic midfield slots, artificially boosting the hold-up section without it containing true hold-up specialists. With Moon Chime dictating alone at a fair but not suicidal clip on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours horses who can genuinely travel prominently — those who secure the early slots behind the leader will have first run at every hurdle in the home straight and avoid the trouble likely to materialise through the congested midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Chime sets a steady-to-fair gallop and the prominent slots are cleanly filled by Newtown Rambler, Louis Veron and Howth, who travel close to pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Moon Chime's lone front-running creates a single-file procession where the first wave of prominent runners dictate their own fate and attack from two out, leaving the displaced midfield pack too much to do on Good ground. Horses with a genuine ability to race close and quicken off a fair pace hold the clearest advantage, and the sequence riders among the prominent group will be hardest to peg back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Moon Chime, untroubled and dictating her own fractions, rolls along at a pace that suits her stamina and the chasing pack never lands a blow.
scenarios.body: A solo, uncontested lead on Good ground over an honest trip can become a difficult target to reel in when the chaser pack is disorganised by overcrowding, and Moon Chime has two recent wins to her name at this trip range. Those who travel closest behind her — Newtown Rambler, Howth — give themselves the best each-way chance, but the leader's comfort could prove the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough in the middle stages to string out the genuine prominent types and leave them vulnerable to a late surge from the back.
scenarios.body: Charlus and Pigeon House are the only true hold-up runners in the field, meaning any late finish would rely on them or the genuinely displaced midfielders finding clear air — a far from certain outcome given how congested the midfield will be. Good ground does not typically produce a swamping finish at Market Rasen, and the lack of real hold-up pedigree in the back section limits the chances of a mass late sweep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Shuffles the Pack
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners contest early position aggressively and the pace fragments, causing errors at hurdles and opening the race up for a fortunate survivor.
scenarios.body: With so many horses wanting to be prominent, bumping and crowding at the early hurdles is a genuine risk that could unsettle fancied runners and produce a race where a fresh or well-handicapped outsider finds daylight. High Fibre, just eight days since his last run and wearing a visor, could benefit from positional carnage given his course-type form, while any incident among the lead group could gift a place to an unconsidered runner.

watchPoints.text: Moon Chime's lead — if she bowls along unchallenged through the first mile the entire race shape depends on whether the chasing pack can close the gap at the second-last; if she still has a length margin there, she may be very hard to catch.

Louis Veron with Harry Skelton is the most potent jockey-trainer booking in the race and merits close watching jumping off — if Skelton places him just behind Moon Chime with a smooth passage, his recent winning streak makes him the most likely to pounce from a prominent position.

Newtown Rambler's hat-trick form is outstanding but Oakley Brown is a 5lb claimer against seasoned professionals in a 13-runner field; watch whether he can get the position he needs cleanly at the first two hurdles, where crowding could cost him several lengths.

The congested midfield group — Continuance, Morning Mayhem, Squeezebox and High Fibre — are all natural front-of-the-pack horses stuck in an unnatural position; watch for interference and shuffling at the downhill hurdles where the field bunches, as this is where the race could unravel for at least one fancied runner.

Charlus and Pigeon House are the only genuine hold-up horses and will be conspicuous by their position at the back of the field; if Good ground produces a truly even-paced contest with no late fade from the leaders, neither is likely to get competitive — but a strong gallop that burns out the prominent pack would flip the script entirely.

races.name: Betway Summer Plate Handicap Steeple Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mahons Glory
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, OR 143, trained by Dylan Cunha with two wins from nine runs on similar going; has the class advantage in this field and a recent course success over 22f backs his claims strongly if he holds his pitch — jockey Lee Edwards has ridden him to both recent wins.|

runners_data.name: Soul Icon
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride on this nine-year-old for Keiran Burke, who has a quiet recent record (0/7 in 14 days); 99 days off the track is a notable freshness flag, and four career pulls-ups or refusals in recent history demand jumping confidence at this venue.|

runners_data.name: Riaan
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott is firing (10/59 in 14 days) and Danny Gilligan partners this Irish raider who won over 21f good ground; form has tailed off (P014-0) and a recent mark of 15th over 20f good raises questions about consistency, but the trainer angle merits respect.|

runners_data.name: Gunsight Ridge
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old for Mike Sowersby who is 1/2 in the 14-day window — a positive yard stat; best form came on good (3rd recently) but five of his last five runs have come on soft or heavy ground and this firmer surface is a legitimate concern for a horse of his age and profile.|

runners_data.name: Breizh River
runners_data.note: Tristan Davidson has had three winners from eleven runners recently and this eight-year-old arrives on a strong sequence — wins at 21f and 22f good ground are directly relevant; headgear (tongue-tie and visor) suggests he needs restraining, and a 20-day turnaround is a plus.|

runners_data.name: Pour Les Filles
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners this Mickey Bowen-trained mare who has back-to-back thirds on good ground at 21f — consistent without winning, and headgear (tongue-tie and pads) indicates she needs help switching off; the Bowen family double-runner angle (also Queensbury Boy) is worth tracking for in-yard intelligence.|

runners_data.name: Queensbury Boy
runners_data.note: A genuine up-with-the-pace type by nature who won over 25f good ground last time; however, the overcrowded prominent group means he is likely to find himself posted further back than ideal, compromising his ability to exert his natural forward influence in the race.|

runners_data.name: Baltic Bird
runners_data.note: One of only two genuine hold-up horses in the field, and he has course form at 24f and 25f on good ground — 15 of his last 15 runs have come on good, making him the best-ground specialist in the race; Pat O'Brien's 5lb claim is a bonus on OR 126.|

runners_data.name: Kingston Narcissus
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton is an elite jockey who will manage any positional compromise better than most — the horse has won at 20f good and ran second twice recently; by nature a front-end horse, he will likely find himself squeezed back, which blunts his best chance but Skelton's handling could minimise the damage.|

runners_data.name: In The Air
runners_data.note: Five wins on good ground make In The Air perfectly suited to today's conditions, and he was second over 21f soft last time; a natural pace-hungry style pushed into the midfield pack by congestion is a real inconvenience for Ciaran Gethings, who will need to find gaps off a sustainable gallop.|

runners_data.name: St Faz
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley sends this six-year-old over from Ireland with two wins from nine runs in 14 days — a busy yard; his form at 16f distances (four of five recent runs were sub-17f) makes this step up to 2m5½f a significant unknown, and he's been out of the frame more often than not.|

runners_data.name: Stans The Man
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard's nine-year-old has a genuine stamina profile — second over 28f good and third over 29f good — so the trip holds no fears; pushed back against his natural prominent inclination, he may thrive if this develops into a genuine endurance test in the final mile.|

runners_data.name: King Roly
runners_data.note: The other confirmed hold-up type, trained by Mickey Bowen (who also runs Pour Les Filles and Queensbury Boy); four wins on good ground from 12 course-suitable runs is strong, and Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim on OR 120 makes him well-treated — naturally suited to coming late if the pace-scenario unfolds.|

runners_data.name: Nickelforce
runners_data.note: Ben Case's seven-year-old arrives having won two of his last five on good ground at around 20-22f — strong recent form; a front-end runner by nature who will not secure that position today given the congestion, and J M Quinlan will need to ride a waiting race that may not fully complement the horse's best form.|

races.paceDynamic: Mahons Glory is the confirmed pace-setter here and, critically, faces no serious pressure for the lead — Soul Icon, Breizh River, Pour Les Filles and Gunsight Ridge are the next most prominent but none profiles as a genuine challenger for the front position, meaning Mahons Glory can control tempo from flag to finish on good ground over 2m5½f. With a solo front-runner setting a measured, sustainable gallop, this shapes as a thorough stamina test rather than a speed-from-the-front affair, and horses who can travel prominently in behind and pounce in the final mile are the primary beneficiaries. The field holds significantly more prominent-type runners than the map can accommodate — Queensbury Boy, Kingston Narcissus, In The Air, St Faz, Stans The Man and Nickelforce are all natural up-with-the-pace horses who will be competing for a limited number of positions in the prominent group, meaning several will be shuffled back against their will. The net result is a race shape that most strongly favours a genuine hold-up horse or a true stayer who can be produced with a sustained run from off the pace — Baltic Bird and King Roly sit most naturally in that profile and are the types this shape is built for.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mahons Glory Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mahons Glory gets a clean lead and dictates a measured, uncontested gallop, allowing him to conserve energy through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Mahons Glory's OR of 143 and recent course win give him the class and confidence to dictate on good ground; his jockey Lee Edwards knows him well and can control fractions without burning him out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo set by Mahons Glory is just fast enough to stretch the prominent scramble, opening the door for genuine hold-up runners to close strongly in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: With numerous prominent types crowding the chase pack and possibly pushing the pace beyond comfort, horses who have been quietly held up are in prime position to finish past a tiring melee.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaos Delivers Dark Horse
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of pace horses causes scrimmaging mid-race, unsettling rhythms and producing an unsuspected winner from the crowded prominent-to-midfield group.
scenarios.body: One of the redistributed horses — most likely Kingston Narcissus or Queensbury Boy — manages to find a comfortable berth just behind Mahons Glory and gets first run when the leader tires.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grinds Out A Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If the combination of 2m5½f on good ground and a competitive pack behind Mahons Glory turns this into an extended stamina examination from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Stans The Man's form over marathon trips (2nd over 28f, 3rd over 29f) and Riaan's single course win at 21f suit a long-run-in grind, while lighter-weighted or speed-reliant types empty out.

watchPoints.text: Baltic Bird and King Roly — the only two natural hold-up horses in the field — will be the chief beneficiaries if Mahons Glory sets a truly uncontested pace; watch whether they get a clean passage through the final turn where Market Rasen's layout can cause bunching.

Queensbury Boy, Kingston Narcissus and In The Air will all be jostling for the same prominent positions early; a scrimmage or jumping error among this group in the first mile could have a knock-on effect that alters the entire shape of the race.

Mahons Glory is 10 years old and carrying 168lbs — if he has done more work than usual in the lead and the weight tells from the second-last fence, the race could open up dramatically for anything held up behind him.

Soul Icon's record includes multiple non-completions (U, B in recent form) and 99 days off the track; a jumping mistake or early exit from a prominent position would further compress an already crowded chase group directly behind the leader.

Market Rasen's home straight is short and undulating — horses who are in the first four or five rounding the final bend have a significant advantage; any runner still making ground at the last fence will find the run-in tests their stamina rather than their speed.

races.name: Betway Bet The Responsible Way Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1-1-5 in last five) with course-distance winning experience on good; Stuart Edmunds yard is 0/1 in the last 14 days, but the horse's prominent style is tailor-made for solo front-running here — her STYLE_FIT tag reflects she is slightly out of profile against her OR, but this race shape is unusually accommodating for her.|

runners_data.name: Sun Art
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien firing at 1/9 in past fortnight, which is an important stable flag; prominent racer with solid placed form on good ground and five career places from 11 similar-going starts — this trip and surface suit and the 51-day freshener may sharpen him.|

runners_data.name: Jolie Coeur Allen
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam's hold-up performer who has a course win at 17f on good and placed at 17f on soft — the trip and going are right; tongue-tie applied, 22 days since last run and 0/7 for trainer in the past 14 days tempers enthusiasm, but Richie McLernon is an able partner for a late challenge.|

runners_data.name: No More Bolero
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes the ride on a hold-up type with three wins from 15 good-ground starts and a strong recent record (won last time 31 days ago); James Owen's 8/48 strike rate over 14 days is substantial positive trainer context — best on good, best at 16-17f, this is firmly in his wheelhouse.|

runners_data.name: Forest Spirit
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a top-tier jockey and will maximise whatever position he can find, but this is a genuine rear-tracking type re-mapped to midfield due to field congestion; the horse's best form has come over longer trips (20f+) and on softer surfaces, and the STYLE_FIT flag is reinforced by a form string showing inconsistency — expect him to need plenty to go right.|

races.paceDynamic: Hello Sweety is the sole confirmed front-runner in this five-runner field and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, she should dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front — sustainable rather than scorching over 2m½f on good ground at Market Rasen. Sun Art is a prominent-racing type who will likely slot in behind her and give some shape to the early pace, while Jolie Coeur Allen, No More Bolero, and the redistributed Forest Spirit will be held up to varying degrees. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get to the rear in a clean arrangement — Forest Spirit is a genuine closer mapped to midfield due to the congestion behind, meaning she is unlikely to get the clean, wide-open run her style ideally demands. With Hello Sweety controlling the tempo unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer or a single well-timed close-range finisher who can track the pace and pounce — not a deep hold-up merchant dependent on a strong pace to reel back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hello Sweety Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety settles in front at a fair clip and none of the hold-up horses can generate enough momentum to close.
scenarios.body: Hello Sweety dictates every yard from flag to finish, setting a fair but not punishing gallop, and Sun Art tracks in second before both are challenged off the home turn; the horse with the stamina and jumping fluency to stay prominent throughout benefits enormously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Her In
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety's gallop is honest enough to ensure she ties up late, allowing a hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: No More Bolero or Jolie Coeur Allen, held up in the body of the small field, gets a clear run into the straight and picks off a tiring leader; both have winning form on good ground at this sort of trip and carry strong jockey bookings.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate enough for a prominent-to-midfield tracker to coast into contention off the final hurdle and quicken.
scenarios.body: Sun Art, sitting handy and fresh off 51 days, finds a good position behind Hello Sweety and produces a smooth challenge approaching the last, turning strong trainer form into a race-day performance; this shape suits a horse with tactical speed over a patient closer.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Positions
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors or significant interference reshuffle the field and no single horse controls the gallop cleanly.
scenarios.body: A muddled tempo with horses out of position creates a pocket-and-switch finish where Forest Spirit, despite being squeezed out of her natural rear-tracking role, benefits from a disjointed race; the scenario depends heavily on out-of-role runners finding clear daylight, making it the least likely of the four shapes.

watchPoints.text: Watch Hello Sweety at the first couple of hurdles — if she jumps fluently and opens up early, she could build an unassailable lead that the small field never collectively organises to challenge.

No More Bolero's last-time winner status under Harry Cobden combined with James Owen's 8/48 14-day trainer strike rate makes him the most significant market mover to monitor — any drifting odds will be informative.

Jolie Coeur Allen's tongue-tie application is worth noting as a first-time equipment change that can alter early pace behaviour — if she travels better than usual in the first mile, the hold-up plan may be abandoned.

With only five runners, any jumping error or interference on the turn out of the back straight is magnified — Forest Spirit in particular has little room to manoeuvre if caught in a pocket behind the leaders.

Sun Art is 51 days off a run with one of the hotter 14-day trainer records in this field — watch the market from opening show to off, as O'Brien horses backed from a break often tell a story beforehand.

races.name: Read Paul Townend's Betway Blog Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Catchim
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer with a win and seven placings from 15 similar-going starts, trained by Charles & Adam Pogson; natural hold-up runner who will need a truly run race to land a blow, which this race shape is unlikely to provide, but strong form profile makes him the most dangerous of the late finishers if things unravel up front.

runners_data.name: Dream Jet
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's eight-year-old is lightly raced over this shorter trip and prefers to come from off the pace, yet his Good-ground placing record (two wins, six places from 11 starts) is solid; 42 days off the track is worth noting, and he may need to race closer than ideal given the hold-up traffic, which could actually aid him if he tracks the pace more prominently than usual.

runners_data.name: Sledgehammer
runners_data.note: OR 94 from the Farrell yard, returning 15 days after his last run; a genuine hold-up horse who finds himself mapped to midfield because the rear is saturated with closers, meaning he will almost certainly race out of his preferred position and that positional compromise must temper expectations in a shape where he cannot hunt down a leader running away at his own pace.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: David Bridgwater's runner brings headgear (p) and has a strong Good-ground record — two wins and four places from 12 starts at the track — and was last seen winning 11 days ago, which is a fitness tick; a true hold-up horse, he's pushed into the midfield group on the map, and while his recent form is the best of the closers, the likely controlled pace makes it hard to see him producing a devastating late run.

runners_data.name: Prospect House
runners_data.note: The key pace figure in this race, wearing a visor and ridden by claimer William Maggs (3lb), who adds significant weight advantage; sole confirmed front-runner who should secure an uncontested lead, and his Good-ground placing record (two wins, ten places from 15 starts) underlines he handles conditions well, though the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that he is likely to be doing more work than natural in a field this deep.

runners_data.name: Huit Reflets
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old for Mark Walford wearing a visor, who has run twice in the last 11 days and appears in good order; a prominent type who can sit just off Prospect House's shoulder and is one of only two horses naturally suited to tracking the likely leader, making him a key player in the dominant scenario despite a more modest Good-ground record of one win and two places from seven attempts.

runners_data.name: Mr McWhinny
runners_data.note: Wears tongue tie for T Ellis and has an excellent Good-ground base (13 from 15 starts run on similar ground), but has not won from this hold-up style and is mapped to midfield rather than his true rearward position, meaning he faces both a positional and pace-shape challenge; his 35-day absence and moderate OR of 78 make it difficult to construct a strong winning argument.

runners_data.name: Fox Wallace
runners_data.note: Ella Pickard's runner is back just six days after his last outing and has accumulated question marks (three pulled-up runs in recent history) alongside modest finishing positions; a genuine hold-up horse shifted into midfield on the map, and his form string of PP-P57 offers little confidence that he can overcome the structural disadvantage of a slow pace in a crowded rear, even on familiar Good ground.

races.paceDynamic: Prospect House is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival prepared to pressurise from the outside, is expected to dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m1f trip on Good ground at Market Rasen. The field is heavily populated with hold-up types — Sledgehammer, Most Wanted, Mr McWhinny, Fox Wallace and Catchim all want to come from off the pace — meaning the rear will be congested and several of those will be forced to race closer to the pace than they'd naturally prefer. Dream Jet and Huit Reflets offer the most credible prominent challenge to Prospect House, though neither is a natural front-runner. This race shape — a controlled, modest gallop set by a single leader — heavily favours horses who can track close to the pace and produce a clean jump-by-jump performance, disadvantaging the numerous hold-up types who will struggle to find the clear passage and late momentum a truly run race would generate. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear, and Sledgehammer, Most Wanted, Mr McWhinny and Fox Wallace are the runners most at risk of being crowded out and forced to race wide or closer than ideal, with Prospect House and Huit Reflets best placed to secure their natural positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prospect House Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Prospect House bowls along uncontested at a controlled pace and the hold-up horses fail to muster a coordinated late challenge.
scenarios.body: Prospect House sets a manageable tempo through the early stages, clears his fences fluently and simply quickens away from his rivals in the straight before the closers can organise; with so many hold-up types crowded at the rear and forced out of their comfort zones, no single finisher generates enough momentum to reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit Front Late
scenarios.trigger: If Huit Reflets or Dream Jet tracks Prospect House throughout and produces a sharper jump at the last to collar him.
scenarios.body: A pace-perfect round of jumping from one of the prominent trackers allows them to take over approaching the final fence, with the steady gallop meaning stamina is not truly tested; horses who have raced handily without over-committing are rewarded, while the hold-up brigade are again denied the truly run race they need.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a jumping error by Prospect House bunches the field and creates a sprint finish that suits a fast-finishing hold-up type.
scenarios.body: A sudden change of pace or incident at a fence compresses the field in the home straight, allowing one of the better-credentialled closers — most likely Catchim or Most Wanted, both with solid Good-ground form — to pick through tired rivals; Most Wanted's recent course form and Catchim's placing record in similar conditions make them the most dangerous of the hold-up contingent if this scenario materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Pace Blows Field Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Huit Reflets or a redistributed hold-up type presses Prospect House aggressively early and the tempo becomes genuinely searching.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop stretches the field from an early stage and tests the stamina of front-runners, potentially leaving them vulnerable to a battle-hardened stayer who has settled in behind; however, given the modest pace evidence and the redistribution of true hold-up types away from the rear, this scenario requires several things to go wrong simultaneously and is the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Prospect House — if he meets his fences cleanly from the front, his rivals have very little time to organise a challenge in a 2m1f contest; any jumping error early could compromise his entire race.

Sledgehammer, Most Wanted and Fox Wallace — all genuine hold-up horses forced towards midfield, creating a risk of crowding and interference on the final turn; jockeys on these three should be watched for positional disputes.

Catchim and Dream Jet — both are Hold-Up types with strong Good-ground records who will be squeezed for room if the rear bunches; watch whether their jockeys elect to switch wide early to avoid traffic.
Huit Reflets — having run 11 days ago, any sign of fatigue in the final circuit or a loose jump at a key fence could rapidly change the complexion of the race and open it up for the hold-up brigade.

William Maggs (3lb claim) on Prospect House — the combination of a front-runner and a claiming jockey should be monitored for jumping accuracy; a novice error under pressure from Huit Reflets could flip the whole race shape.

races.name: Betway Boosts Handicap Steeple Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Special John
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner in excellent recent form (won 38 days ago over 24f on good), likely to get a soft lead; his prominent style fits perfectly here, though the step up to 3m and a possible tactical crawl could be his only threat.

runners_data.name: Yes Day
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill (4 wins from 14 over 14 days — trainer in decent form), has placed twice on good ground at similar trips, and blinkers suggest he needs cover before delivering his effort late.

runners_data.name: Giovanni Change
runners_data.note: Veteran of 11 yet remarkably consistent on good ground (ten runs, three wins, seven places at similar going); prominent style suits this shape well but at OR 107 and age 11 he needs things to fall right, and trainer is quiet (0/17 over 14 days).

runners_data.name: Sir Carnegie
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced six-year-old in excellent form (42-311), winning his last two; his natural prominent style is well-suited to sit just off Special John's pace, and Shane Fenelon's 5lb claim gives a meaningful weight advantage, though most wins have come on softer ground.

runners_data.name: Redbridge Rambler
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1/24f/good, 42 days ago) who naturally wants to race prominently but has been bumped back by the number of pace horses in this field; the visor goes on and he has strong course-going figures (12 from 15 on good), meaning he could still push forward if the pace from Special John isn't severe.

runners_data.name: You Did
runners_data.note: Pulled up last time out and has a mixed record on good ground (1 win, 1 place from 5 on good), making his form profile more fragile than his style would suggest; Patrick Wadge takes the ride and the hood may sharpen focus, but the question mark over his recent run is significant.

runners_data.name: Millena Agent
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature, shown here in midfield only because the map is crowded with rear-rankers; has only three chase runs on record with no wins (0W2P), and trainer Walford is out of form (0/17 over 14 days), making a first-time win a tall order from this position.

races.paceDynamic: Special John is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only one genuine pace-setter in a field of seven over three miles on good ground, he is likely to dictate at a sensible, sustainable gallop rather than be pressed into a war of attrition. Giovanni Change and Sir Carnegie are both prominent-style horses who will look to sit close to the tempo, creating a compact lead group rather than a strung-out field, which means the race is unlikely to fall apart tactically. Yes Day and You Did are genuine hold-up horses operating from their natural position, though they will need Special John to stretch things sufficiently to bring their staying power into play late in a three-mile trip. This shape — a controlled, measured pace set by one front-runner with a tight prominent cluster — most strongly favours hold-up horses with genuine staying ability who can pick off tiring rivals in the final half-mile, provided the gallop has been honest enough to expose those who travelled too freely. The field contains more prominent-type horses than the map can accommodate: Redbridge Rambler and Millena Agent are genuine pace-hungry types who have been pushed back on the map, and Special John and Giovanni Change are most likely to actually secure their natural position at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Special John sets a steady-to-honest gallop and the prominent cluster travels well but ties up in the closing stages, leaving the race to be won from behind.
scenarios.body: Special John dictates without undue pressure, Giovanni Change and Sir Carnegie track closely, but three miles on good ground exposes any vulnerabilities in those who burned energy racing up with the pace; hold-up horses with stamina find their stride late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely honest early and Special John sustains it long enough to crack the hold-up horses before they can produce a telling run.
scenarios.body: Special John's prominent riders Giovanni Change and Sir Carnegie prove the strongest staying types on the day, lasting home as the hold-up horses fail to bridge the gap in time; the good ground suits those who raced efficiently close to the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Unexpected Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is falsely slow early and a midfield or rear horse produces a dramatic turn of foot in the home straight.
scenarios.body: A stop-start tempo scrambles the form entirely, rewarding the horse with the sharpest response off slow fractions; Redbridge Rambler, racing out of natural role but with genuine pace, could be best placed to exploit a dash for home if the race suddenly quickens.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Special John encounters minimal pressure, dictates an uncontested tempo, and rations his effort so perfectly that he simply outstays all pursuers.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to challenge him for the lead, Special John controls every fraction and simply never gives the hold-up horses enough pace to aim at; his good-ground form figures (two wins on good) underpin this possibility.

watchPoints.text: Special John sets a very slow tempo — if he dawdles in front with no pressure, the race could turn into a sprint finish that blunts the advantage of genuine stayers like Yes Day.

Redbridge Rambler wears the visor for the first time and is a natural front-runner; watch whether Freddie Keighley pushes him forward early against the pace map — if he does, Special John's uncontested lead disappears and the whole shape shifts.
You Did was pulled up last time out (13 days ago) and ran well below expectations — his jumping and confidence will be under scrutiny at every fence early in the race.

Giovanni Change's age (11) makes stamina in the final half-mile a genuine question at 3m on good ground, even given his strong place record — watch whether he fades from two out having travelled well for much of the trip.

Sir Carnegie has won his last two but both victories came with some give in the ground; the step up to 3m on good going is a new question for the six-year-old and his jumping accuracy over the extra fences deserves close attention early.

races.name: Watch Live Racing At Betway Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Glory And Honour
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up performer with multiple wins at this trip on good ground, ridden by claiming jockey Tom Midgley; at OR 111 he is the top-weight and has the class but needs things to fall right from the back.|

runners_data.name: Prince Quattro
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride on this Owen-trained seven-year-old, whose sole win on good ground came over 2m — today's 2m4½f on good is an open question; strong form placing record gives each-way claims from off the pace.|

runners_data.name: Belvedere Blast
runners_data.note: Wears a visor for Adrian Keatley and has placed in both recent runs on good at this trip (two thirds at 3m); the amateur claimer Oakley Brown is a slight concern in a competitive 13-runner field.|

runners_data.name: Arnie Moon
runners_data.note: Consistent six-year-old with a win at 2m on good — steps up significantly in distance today; Callum Pritchard partners and Tickle's stable is in decent form over the 14-day window, so trip stamina is the key query.|

runners_data.name: Vivid Pink
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter, Alan King's seven-year-old has won twice over 2m4½f+ on good and Bellamy can dictate from the front with zero pressure — hood worn and an uncontested lead is his best friend today.|

runners_data.name: Ballygeary
runners_data.note: Mike Sowersby's nine-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse that the map places in midfield due to field congestion; off just 20 days, he has struggled in recent outings (OR 107) and his trainer's short 14-day strike-rate of 1/2 is too small to read into.|

runners_data.name: Twist Of Fatecatch
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes over on this Mulholland six-year-old who has placed four times in the last five over this sort of distance on good or soft; a natural prominent racer who should find a comfortable seat just behind the leader.|

runners_data.name: Shesonnet
runners_data.note: Five-year-old returned just two days ago and that extreme freshness is an immediate flag; placed four times including twice at 2m on good, she is a hold-up type forced into a midfield slot, and any leftover tiredness from her mid-week run could cost her late.|

runners_data.name: Oneinthewell
runners_data.note: Both recent runs produced seconds and Jonathan Burke is an experienced partner; a genuine come-from-behind type that the redistribution places in midfield — his best chance is if the pace blows up late, but the going and the controlled tempo work against that.|

runners_data.name: Nottodaybobo
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on good ground at 2m, and Joshua Thompson (5) takes the ride for Hammond; a natural hold-up horse shuffled into midfield on the map, yet two wins on this going at this track-style gives him a genuine profile for a late challenge if gaps open.|

runners_data.name: Saxon Cross
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds' six-year-old has an entirely blank win record on good ground across seven runs (0W1P) and Saxon Cross steps up from shorter trips; the redistribution to midfield is somewhat fitting given his lack of finishing kick on this surface.|

runners_data.name: Modern Style
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with two wins on good ground and a strong recent profile (011-23); James Davies partners for Nigel Hawke, and at the minimum weight of 153lbs the age and weight allowance give him an edge — a horse to follow as conditions suit even if he must race in a midfield pack rather than at the front where he is most effective.|

runners_data.name: Mojo Ego
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's six-year-old bounced back with a win 17 days ago at 2m on good, so fitness is fine; a hold-up horse mapped to midfield, he will need that last win to have been a springboard and a clean run from the pack to be involved.|

races.paceDynamic: Vivid Pink is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, with no natural rival to press him from the start, Tom Bellamy can dictate an honest but uncontested gallop across the 2m4½f trip on good ground at Market Rasen. Behind him, Twist Of Fatecatch is the likeliest horse to sit in a close-up prominent position, while the bulk of the field — Glory And Honour, Prince Quattro, Belvedere Blast, Arnie Moon and many others — are genuine hold-up types who will track from midfield or further back. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the map can place at the rear: Ballygeary, Shesonnet, Oneinthewell, Nottodaybobo, Saxon Cross, Modern Style and Mojo Ego are all true come-from-behind types redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning they will be bunched in a tight, competitive pack rather than enjoying clear daylight. With a single, uncontested pace-setter controlling a sound gallop on a fair surface, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently in Vivid Pink's slipstream or possess a high cruising speed that allows them to make smooth headway from midfield from two out — authentic hold-up horses who need a truly searching pace to be set will need late fortune.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Vivid Pink Controls, Stays Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Vivid Pink travels comfortably at the head of affairs and Bellamy holds enough in reserve to fend off challengers from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Vivid Pink has back-to-back wins over this trip on good ground and faces zero pace pressure today, allowing Bellamy to conserve energy and quicken when asked late; his STYLE_FIT tag reflects the mapping rather than a genuine concern since leading is his actual role.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Vivid Pink sets a pace that is just honest enough to crack in the final half-mile and a horse racing prominently behind him picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Twist Of Fatecatch has the profile to sit close to the pace at this trip, and Harry Cobden will be positioned to pounce if Vivid Pink fades from the last; Prince Quattro, trained by James Owen who has a strong recent record, has the form credentials to close from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough through the middle stages to bring genuine closers into play from off the bridle at the second-last.
scenarios.body: The redistributed midfield cluster means many true hold-up types will be racing in a congested group and will need clear gaps to appear in the straight; Nottodaybobo has winning form on this going and at this trip and could be the sharpest finisher if traffic clears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Interference
scenarios.trigger: If the large, tightly-packed midfield bunch causes jumping interference or fallers that scramble the race entirely.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners over hurdles and many genuine hold-up types forced into an unnaturally compact mid-race position, the risk of costly traffic problems or a fall disrupting fancied horses is higher than usual; a horse with a wide, unencumbered passage such as Arnie Moon or Modern Style could benefit from luck in running.

watchPoints.text: Shesonnet ran just two days ago — monitor for any signs of race fatigue or listlessness in the parade ring before the off, as a hold-up horse forced to race in a tightly bunched midfield is the worst scenario for a horse that may be carrying residual tiredness.

The 13-runner field contains a mass of hold-up types compressed into a compact mid-race bunch — watch for potential jumping interference or crowding as the field approaches the third-last hurdle where the course narrows and gaps close.

Vivid Pink's STYLE_FIT flag relates to the mapping process and not his form — if Bellamy elects not to lead for any reason (slow start, rival jumping ahead), the entire pace shape collapses and the race becomes far more chaotic than projected.

Modern Style at 153lbs carries a significant weight advantage over the top two in the market and James Davies has form on good ground — watch the market moves in the final 30 minutes as any market support for this lightly weighted four-year-old could be informative.

James Owen saddles both Prince Quattro and Oneinthewell — watch which of the two is better fancied in the betting ring, as the trainer's recent 14-day strike-rate of 8/48 suggests a live stable and dual runners often signal one is more fancied than the other.
